absent: Numeric values of preallocation counts, kernel boundary, maximum user tables, table fanout and page and huge page sizes.
Ownership and build conditions selecting alternate variants for user prepopulation, second level reclamation, address translation, clone level and vsyscall setup.
Semantics of constructor and destructor hooks, paravirt allocation hooks, swapper table layout and user top table translation.
Lock type and initialization of the pgd list guard and full synchronization rules for concurrent table walks.
Error and warning macro behavior, presence and leaf and none predicates, and TLB flush helper internals.
Early option registration strings for allocator reserve, top reservation, protection keys and isolation modes.
Protection key bit positions, bits per key, write disable mask and hardware enable detection.
Shadow stack encodings, generic make writable and saved dirty handling, and virtual area flag values.
Fixed map ceiling type, vmalloc region bounds, low memory limit and physical validity predicate.
Allocation flag values, kernel mapping permissions, vsyscall address and level constants, and invlpgb limits.

findings.text: Top level table creation allocates a new table, preallocates kernel and user lower tables, records the result in the address space descriptor and reports failure with a null return, while release tears down preallocated tables, runs destructor hooks and frees the top level.

Creation advances through top allocation, kernel preallocation, user preallocation and paravirt reservation, where each later failure unwinds only earlier successful stages before releasing the top level.
Constructor invocation and population of fresh tables occur while holding the global pgd_lock guard, so concurrent walkers never observe a half populated table, with release before successful return.

A single top slot is torn down only when its entry is nonzero, in which case the slot is cleared first and then the referenced lower table is released with paravirt notification, table release and address space counter decrement.

Teardown iterates the fixed count of preallocated kernel slots and, when isolation support is compiled and the CPU advertises the isolation feature, additionally iterates the fixed count of user shadow slots offset from the kernel boundary.

Prepopulation descends to middle levels anchored at zero address and installs one preallocated table per slot, seeding contents from the global table for slots at or above the kernel boundary before linking each table into its parent.

One user shadow variant copies each table from the corresponding user view of the global table starting at the kernel boundary and links it into the user middle level, while the alternate variant performs no action.

Entry update helpers for small, large and huge levels report whether the proposed entry differs from the current one and store the new entry only when a difference exists and the caller indicates dirtiness.

Large and huge access updates require address alignment to the corresponding huge size and avoid explicit TLB maintenance when making an entry more permissive, relying on fault handling with at most a spurious fault.
Youth helpers at three table levels return prior youthfulness, checking the young indicator first and clearing the accessed bit atomically only when previously young.

Youth clearing for the smallest level never flushes the TLB, treating later flushing by context switch or virtual memory activity as sufficient and accepting a small risk of mistaken reclaim of hot pages.

Large youth clearing flushes exactly one huge range when the entry was young, one large invalidate path establishes an invalid entry without flushing because access and dirty state can no longer change, and the huge invalidate path establishes an invalid entry then flushes one huge range.
Large clear and invalidate paths enforce huge alignment and warn when invalidating a non present entry, treating such calls as caller contract violations.
Early 32 bit setup can reserve top virtual space by rounding the request down to a middle level boundary and lowering the fixed map ceiling, and must run before any fixed mapping is established.

Fourth level huge establishment always reports lack of support and fourth level huge clearing does nothing, while lower huge clearing removes the entry only when it is currently a leaf and reports whether removal occurred.

Reclamation of a middle entry detaches its lower table, issues a kernel range flush to reach cached walks, destroys each populated descendant descriptor, then frees the detached table and reports success.
Kernel range flushing prepares flush state with page granularity and an invalid generation marker, then selects a full flush when the normalized end indicates everything and a ranged flush otherwise.

Kernel full and ranged flushes prefer broadcast invalidation instructions when the CPU advertises them and otherwise broadcast a flush routine to every CPU, with hardware ranged flushing split into bounded chunks followed by a synchronization barrier.
Kernel range flush setup holds a preemption guard while preparing flush state, preventing migration or preemption between initialization and dispatch choice.

One second level reclamation variant detaches the lowest table, flushes paging caches for one page, destroys the descriptor and reports success, while the alternate variant does no teardown and only reports whether the entry is already empty.
Make writable helpers divert shadow stack areas to dedicated transformations and otherwise apply the generic make writable transformation followed by clearing of saved dirty state.
Validation of zapped entries at three levels warns when a shadow stack encoding appears in an area lacking the shadow stack flag, noting that older hardware can rarely set dirty on a read only entry.
The 32 bit allocator reserve defaults to one hundred twenty eight megabytes and the fixed map ceiling defaults to just below the top of the 32 bit space.
Two early boot options adjust the allocator reserve by adding a guard hole to the parsed size and reserve top address space then reinitialize early mappings, each rejecting a missing argument.

Physical translation and virtual validity checks exist in 64 bit and 32 bit forms, distinguishing the kernel image alias from the direct map on 64 bit and using a direct offset with vmalloc and fixed map exclusions on 32 bit, gating validity on frame legitimacy.

The 64 bit translation treats addresses above the kernel map base as image aliases bounded by image size plus a base offset, and lower addresses as direct map aliases, flagging underflow and invalid physical results as programming errors.

The 32 bit translation rejects addresses below the direct map base and inside the vmalloc region once its start is known, rejects fixed map addresses during validity checks, and bounds the frame number by the low memory limit when established.

The access disable mask for a protection key shifts a single disable bit by key index times bits per key, and the initial register value disables access for keys one through fifteen while leaving key zero accessible.

An architecture debug file exposes the initial protection key value as hexadecimal text and accepts a numeric update rejected when it would deny access or writes to key zero, while an early boot option installs a supplied numeric value.
The debug file operations bind read, write and seek handlers to respectively the hexadecimal show routine, the validating store routine and the generic seek routine.
Creation of the protection key debug file runs at initialization time but does nothing unless the CPU advertises operating system protection key support.
Isolation log lines carry a kernel user tables prefix and the isolation specific no track allocation modifier is defined as zero, leaving standard allocation behavior unchanged.
The kernel image clone granularity has two build variants selecting either middle level or lowest level cloning, and an enumeration names those two clone levels.
Isolation mode rests in automatic, forced off or forced on states, where a boot string selects among off, on and automatic values and a separate no option forces off unconditionally.

User table walks start from the user view of the kernel top entry for kernel addresses only, allocate each missing intermediate level as a zeroed untracked kernel page linked with kernel table permissions, and reject user addresses, unexpected large mappings and user marked entries.
The lowest level walk tolerates a large middle mapping only during a late text phase where it clears that mapping first, and otherwise warns and fails instead of descending into it.

One vsyscall variant clones the entry from kernel tables into user tables only when the source entry exists at small granularity and is populated, then marks the user top table for vsyscall access, while the alternate variant does nothing.
